catalog_quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. Besides the data from Santo Domingo Nuxaa shown in (4.2), several other descriptions support the characterization of stress in Mixtec as falling on the first vowel of the couplet. ... In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. As I describe in §4.3, the data from Ixpantepec Nieves supports this same stress placement, on the first syllable of the couplet. Section §4.3.2 also discusses the two analyses of alignment to the right edge of the stem or the left edge of the root. [Table A.2:] San Juan Teita Tei Teit xtj Alta:W

new_statements.locator: Carroll 2015 p. 86 (PDF p. 108), §4.2.1, quoting Josserand 1983:180; Teita listed as survey town in Carroll Table A.2 p. 277
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: lines 5440-5444 and 5498, and extracted text of PDF p. 108 (printed p. 86, §4.2.1) of, read exactly: 'Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.'.. 'In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec.' Verbatim as reported; the '[..]' elides Carroll's run through Ayutla, Jicaltepec, Acatlan, Diuxi, Mixtepec, Atatlahuca, Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala, none of which is Teita. One locator nit: the Table A.2 row 'San Juan Teita Tei Teit xtj Alta:W' is on printed p. 276…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-wide Mixtec generalization (not Teita-specific): the word is built on a disyllabic/bimoraic root 'couplet' and stress falls on the first syllable of that couplet, i.e. root-initial (penultimate in an unaffixed disyllabic word); prefixes and enclitics lie outside the stress domain. No first-hand description of San Juan Teita Mixtec prosody exists to confirm this for the variety.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Teita; Carroll notes variety-specific deviations elsewhere in Mixtec (tone-dependent stress in Ayutla/Molinos/Huajuapan; enclitic effects in Silacayoapan/Alacatlatzala; Atatlahuca penultimate in polysyllables).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the couplet (root/stem template), a word-level statement generalized over Josserand's 120+-town dialect survey, which includes San Juan Teita (code Teit) and Santa María Tataltepec; SIL's Teita primer does not write tone or mention accent, so nothing variety-specific is available.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.x languoid 'Teita-Tataltepec Mixtec' (sanj1282, ISO xtj) covers San Juan Teita and, per Auderset et al.'s subgroup 3.1, Santa María Tataltepec (MixteCoDB doculect tata11, listed there under sant1444). The only primary data in circulation for either town is Josserand's 1983 188-item wordlist (0% tone-marked). The one stress statement whose scope includes Teita is Josserand's family-wide Mixtec couplet generalization (1983:180), not a Teita-specific description; the SIL literacy primer (Barkley & Barkley, San Juan Teita) is Teita-specific but silent on stress and tone.
